title: Create modal depth language and proportional padding algorithm
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: modal surfaces across the product have inconsistent perceived depth and variable padding that breaks alignment in dense tables and dashboards. Goal: establish a concise 'modal depth language' (tokenized elevation + shadow presets) and a proportional padding algorithm so modals scale their internal spacing based on width and density rules. This will make dialogs, confirm modals, and embedded drawer surfaces feel cohesive with the new token system and avoid visual drift between buttons, forms, charts, and tables.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 modal depth tokens (modal-depth-1, modal-depth-2, modal-depth-3) with accompanying shadow/elevation presets and cross-platform CSS variables.
Design and document proportional padding algorithm: rules for small/medium/large breakpoints that scale padding by width and density token (compact, default, spacious).
Create Figma component variants and tokenized styles for all modal sizes and density settings (covers mobile breakpoints).
Engineer-facing spec with concrete CSS variables, JS helper for padding calculation, and migration notes for existing modals. PR ready and linked.
Performance validation: ensure new shadows are GPU-friendly and do not regress rendering in list-heavy pages (tested on dashboard-aggregator page).
Update Console pattern docs and include 3 before/after screenshots in the design docs and a short video showing stacking behavior and focus trap behavior with new depth tokens.
decision_log: Adopt ratio-based padding: basePadding = clamp(12px, 2.5vw, 32px) then multiply by density factor (compact: 0.75, default:1, spacious:1.25).

Use layered shadow presets: modal-depth-1 (subtle), modal-depth-2 (prominent on top of lists), modal-depth-3 (full-screen overlays). Avoid expensive blur spreads; prefer 2 shadow layers with reduced alpha for performance.
Token names confirmed to be prefixed with 'surface.modal.*' to keep taxonomy consistent with existing surface tokens.
review_feedback: Sophia Martinez (PM) 2026-03-04: Ensure accessibility — verify contrast when using deeper shadows and semi-transparent overlays; confirm focus ring spacing doesn't collide with scaled padding.
Diego Rivera (Eng) 2026-03-06: Request: provide fallbacks for older browsers where CSS variables are unavailable and offer static class-based tokens for legacy builds.
Maya Nguyen (Design) 2026-03-08: Suggested reducing top padding on compact modals that host form fields to keep first input above fold on smaller viewports.

2026-03-05: Cross-team sync with Engineering and PM to agree on performance constraints and token naming.

2026-03-11: Accessibility pass scheduled; will run contrast and keyboard navigation tests on staging with new tokens.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: New shadow presets might cause GPU thrashing on pages with many stacked modals/popovers. Mitigation: limit modal-depth-2/3 to top-level overlays only and use flattened drop shadows for nested elements.
Risk: Padding algorithm could introduce layout shift. Mitigation: use clamped values and test with CLS tooling; provide migration guide for manual container overrides.
Risk: Token name collisions during rollout. Mitigation: feature-flagged release and a codemod to help migrate legacy class names to new CSS variables.
